settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: CLICommand.main line 275 re-checks Jenkins.READ after the authenticator and stored-authentication resolution, so the effective identity must also be permitted to read.

getTransportAuthentication() (lines 396-399) returns Jenkins.ANONYMOUS when no transport authentication is present, and Jenkins.checkPermission then denies anonymous users when anonymous read access is disabled.
loadStoredAuthentication() (lines 347-356) falls back to Jenkins.ANONYMOUS on failure, which would fail the later check rather than grant access.
candidates.description: In CLICommand.main (core/src/main/java/hudson/cli/CLICommand.java), the security context is primed with the transport-provided Authentication (line 264: sc.setAuthentication(getTransportAuthentication())), then an initial Jenkins.READ check is executed at line 268 before args4j parses arguments and before the CliAuthenticator/loadStoredAuthentication flow establishes the effective identity (lines 269-273). A second Jenkins.READ check follows at line 275 after authentication. The first check is therefore evaluated against the identity supplied by the CLI transport (for HTTP-tunneled CLI, the HTTP session authentication; for SSH CLI, the SSH user), not against the command-line credentials the user may have supplied via --username/--password. While the duplicate post-authentication check at line 275 keeps this from being a clean bypass of the overall read requirement, the early check can still be satisfied by an identity that is later replaced, and it precedes argument parsing (line 269), so error/exit-code and any command whose run() depends on a side effect of main's ordering are handled under a different Authentication than intended. Root cause is reliance on transport authentication for the first authorization decision combined with the check occurring before the authenticator resolves the final identity.
missing_evidence: No proof that any command's run() can perform a security-sensitive action between line 268 and line 275 without subsequently failing the check at line 275.

The concrete behavior of createCliAuthenticator and the individual CliAuthenticator implementations (e.g., core/src/main/java/hudson/security/CliAuthenticator.java and SSH/HTTP variants) was not fully traced to determine whether the transport identity can differ in a way that changes the outcome.
CLIAction/CliProtocol wiring that sets transportAuth was not read end-to-end.
preconditions: CLI transport supplies a non-anonymous Authentication (e.g., HTTP-tunneled CLI with an authenticated session, or SSH CLI where the SSH principal maps to a Jenkins user).
The invoked CLI command is not LoginCommand/LogoutCommand/HelpCommand so that the READ check at line 268 applies.
candidates.title: CLICommand.main performs an authorization check using transport-level Authentication before CLI/authenticator identity is established

counter_evidence: CLICommand.main is the documented entry point and the default implementation; most commands implement run() and therefore inherit the checks.
No concrete overriding command was identified in the inspected files.
candidates.description: The blanket requirement that nearly all CLI commands require Overall/Read is implemented inside CLICommand.main at lines 267-268 and 274-275 (with explicit exemptions for LoginCommand, LogoutCommand and HelpCommand). Commands that do not route through this main (or that override it, as documented at lines 210-215) would not inherit these checks, since there is no additional central enforcement point visible in this class. The evidence I read shows the check is central to CLICommand.main, but I did not establish that any specific command overrides main in a way that skips it.
missing_evidence: A repository-wide search for commands overriding main() was not performed, and no offending override was observed in the files read.
Whether an independent enforcement layer exists in CLIAction/CliProtocol was not fully traced.
preconditions: A CLICommand implementation overrides main(List,Locale,InputStream,PrintStream,PrintStream) instead of relying on the inherited implementation.
Such an override does not itself call Jenkins.checkPermission(Jenkins.READ).
candidates.title: Jenkins.READ gate for most CLI commands is enforced only in CLICommand.main, so any command overriding main or bypassing it loses the check
